props.name: A reactor doubles the space-time yield
props.note: the O-reactor runs I and I' are data of the preceding paper (ref. 1), included in Table I for comparison (I: 34470 l/hr, H2/CO 3.0 (7.7), 295 °C, preheat 295 °C, 42.2 kg/day, 1.01 kg/l hr; I': 33570 l/hr, 8.5 (10.5), 295 °C, preheat 219 °C, 50.6 kg/day, 1.21 kg/l hr; 1.74 l catalyst); they are not recorded as tests of this source
props.statement: The A reactor produced a much larger amount of methanol than the reactor with no heat exchanger (O reactor), its space-time yield reaching twice that of the O reactor (Exp. I vs Exp. 3), provided the synthesis gas was preheated at a higher temperature (Exps. 2 and 3).

props.name: B reactor smaller gain than A
props.statement: The B reactor also produced more methanol than the O reactor, but the increase was rather low compared with the A reactor (Exp. 1 vs Exp. 6).

props.name: Bcalc from formulae A, C, E, F consistent

evidence.note: 'Bealed's' and 'Bested' are the text layer's readings of Bcalcd; quote withheld: sha256:713006a93f1a39832c18723fee420cdbd5d78234701985f242b57385a0efc490 chars:150

props.statement: The Bcalcd values obtained with h from formulae A, C and E, and with h' from formula F, are consistent with the bed-averaged B̄exp.

props.name: bed resistance about one-third
props.statement: The heat transfer resistance across the catalyst bed is so high as to account for about one-third of the overall heat transfer resistance between the gas in the bed and the gas in the heat exchanger tube.

props.name: Bexp maximum near 0.4 m
props.statement: The experimental cooling coefficient Bexp differs with bed length, with a maximum at about x = 0.4 m.

props.name: C reactor overcools the bed
props.statement: Reliable performance data could not be collected with the C reactor until the incoming gas had been preheated to a much higher temperature (Exp. 7); in this reactor the heat exchanger tube cooled the catalyst bed so much that the bed temperature would decrease too low to allow the progress of the synthesis.

props.name: calculated A-reactor profiles agree
props.statement: The axial temperature profiles calculated for Exp. 4 accord well with the experimental ones, indicating that an adequate Bcalcd from any of the formulae proposed so far can be used for the profile calculation without serious errors.

props.name: profile maxima: upper half in A, bottom in B and C
props.statement: The temperature maximum appears in the upper half of the catalyst bed of the A reactor but near the bottom of the B and C reactors, whose catalyst-inlet temperature is kept considerably lower even with higher preheating; in the A reactor methanol is already produced in the top zone and increases rather monotonously with bed length, whereas in B and C only a small amount appears after more than a quarter of the bed; the B and C profiles are essentially the same in tendency as with the O reactor.

props.name: B/C second passage cools the inlet
props.statement: Owing to the efficient heat transfer between the gases in passages II and III, the temperature profile in the second passage of the B and C exchangers always slopes down markedly in the upper zone, and as a consequence the catalyst inlet temperature is kept comparatively low.

props.name: only the single-tube countercurrent exchanger raises production
props.statement: Among the single-tube countercurrent, double-tube countercurrent and double-tube concurrent heat exchanger tubes, only the first serves to increase methanol production considerably compared with the previously tested reactor with no heat exchanger tube.

props.name: B/C exchangers give no remarkable yield gain unless U23 is lowered in the upper part
props.statement: Taking the most favorable temperature profile into consideration, any remarkable increase in methanol yield is scarcely to be expected from B- and C-type heat exchanger tubes unless special treatment lowers U23 in the upper part of the tubes; this may have resulted in the lower methanol yields of the B and C reactors compared with the A reactor.

props.name: low inlet temperature makes B/C bed profiles like the O reactor's
props.statement: The comparatively low catalyst inlet temperature in the B and C reactors may have led to the axial bed temperature profile being almost identical in tendency with that of the reactor with no heat exchanger tube.

props.name: steep radial temperature rise in the annular bed and at tube surfaces
props.statement: A rough estimate from the available data leads to the expectation of a steep temperature rise in the middle across the annular bed of the A reactor; steep rises are also expected at the outer surface of the heat exchanger tube and at the inner and outer surfaces of the reactor, though nothing decisive can be said.
